user.title: HassStore Tunnel
user.description:
Publish this Home Assistant to the internet through HassStore. Generate an 8-digit bind code on the site first (User Center → Intranet Tunnel → Bind to HA); it is valid for 10 minutes and can be used once.

Please read the HassStore Tunnel Terms of Service before accepting. The main line is located outside mainland China; tunnel configuration, usage and access logs may be transferred to and stored outside the PRC (Article 10 / Appendix B — separate consent).

data.accept_terms: I have read and accept the Terms of Service and the separate cross-border transfer consent

data_description.server_url: Official site by default; use your own address for self-hosted deployments.
data_description.bind_code: One-time code; not needed after binding.

environment.title: Where should the data plane run?
environment.description:
This machine runs HAOS (Supervisor detected). Installing the tunnel client as an app is recommended: separate container, Supervisor watchdog self-healing, and the tunnel survives HA restarts. Tick the option below to run it inside Home Assistant Core instead (simpler, but the tunnel drops when HA restarts).

Note: the bind code is valid for 10 minutes and single-use — use Back to change the site URL or the code.

data.local_client: Run hs-frpc inside the integration (do not install the app)

binary.title: Verify the hs-frpc binary
binary.description:
The in-integration mode downloads and verifies hs-frpc. For security reasons the SHA256 must be provided first — otherwise the integration refuses to download or execute any binary.

Copy the SHA256 for your architecture (amd64 / aarch64) from the official HassStore release page.

data_description.binary_mirror: Official mirror by default; use your own mirror for faster access.

reauth_confirm.description: The device token is no longer valid (disabled, rotated, or the device was deleted on the site). Generate a new bind code and enter it below.

trusted_proxies.title: trusted_proxies must be configured, otherwise login loops forever
trusted_proxies.description:
The tunnel forwards visitor traffic to Home Assistant through the edge Nginx, so HA must treat those proxies as trusted. Otherwise every request appears to come from a proxy address and session validation fails — the symptom is «log in and get bounced back to the login page».

Add the following under `http:` in `/config/configuration.yaml`:

```yaml
http:
  use_x_forwarded_for: true
  trusted_proxies:
    - 172.30.32.0/23
    - 127.0.0.1
    - ::1
```

Then restart Home Assistant. See the app's Documentation page for the proxy addresses of each line/edge.
